prompts.scatteredSix: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: research fixture, ordinary handheld factory tablet photo, horizontal 1536x1024 pixels. Exactly SIX black SOIC-8 integrated circuits lying separately on a worn green textured anti-static ESD mat, roughly two rows of three but slightly irregularly spaced. Each package has four silver leads on each opposing side. Upper row orientations: +12 degrees, -28 degrees, 180 degrees upside down. Lower row: +90 degrees, -130 degrees, +167 degrees. Five chips have three lines of gray laser marking exactly 'SV358' / 'A26' / '0147'. The lower-right chip instead has 'SV385' / 'A26' / '0147'. The lettering rotates physically with each chip. All six packages and leads fully in frame and not touching. Realistic inspection capture rather than studio product shot: slightly soft focus but most lettering readable on zoom, uneven fluorescent illumination, subtle sensor noise, small glare on two packages, low-to-medium contrast laser text. No numbering, no explanatory labels, no artificial bounding boxes, no branding outside the packages. Slight perspective. Keep each chip large enough to inspect, but show realistic surrounding mat.
prompts.trayThirty: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Research fixture: a casual factory incoming-inspection photo taken by an ordinary tablet, landscape 1536x1024 pixels. Show one transparent molded plastic component tray with EXACTLY THIRTY individual black SOT-23 electronic packages, arranged in a complete FIVE-COLUMN by SIX-ROW grid. One tiny three-lead device sits separately in each shallow rectangular transparent pocket. Transparent pocket walls and shiny ridges are clearly present over a green anti-static mat; faint dust, scratches and broad ceiling-light reflections across some pockets, no hands. Top-view with slight perspective, a little softness, moderate sensor noise and slightly uneven exposure, not a studio catalog photograph. All devices have a very short light-gray top marking exactly 'J3', except row five column four which reads 'J8'. Rows two, four and six have devices rotated 180 degrees, so their markings are upside down; other rows upright with small random tilts. Each real chip and text physically rotates as a unit. Most top codes should remain readable upon close inspection but not unnaturally sharp, a few partially affected by thin glare. All thirty pockets visible in frame, no printed row/column numbers, no bounding boxes or annotations, no giant title, no extra objects. Preserve realistic scale of devices, transparent tray, leads and pockets.
prompts.longCode: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Research image, horizontal 1536x1024, imperfect handheld tablet photo of TWO black rectangular flat IC packages with fine silver leads on four sides, separate on a worn green anti-static mat. Upper-left package is tilted about 21 degrees clockwise; lower-right package is rotated about 180 degrees plus 15 degrees, its printed text upside down. Both devices have three laser-etched lines, medium-small rather than huge. First package text exactly 'STM32F103C8T6' / 'GH27B5' / 'TWN 2426'. Second text exactly 'STM32F103C8I6' / 'GH27B5' / 'TWN 2426' (I in place of T in the final code, a deliberate single-character variant). Keep physical leads credible and entire packages in frame. Actual ordinary production inspection capture quality: underexposed in places, low-contrast gray printing on matte black, mild defocus and slight hand-motion softness, visible sensor grain, uneven fluorescent light, a pale diagonal glare across one edge but most lettering still possible to read on close inspection. NOT a pristine studio rendering, NOT perfect razor-sharp text. No annotations, no labels outside chips, no human hands, no title, no watermarks, no PCB.
